correctness.rationale: Fourier diagonalization gives sigma_k^2=2(1-cos(2pi k/n))(1+b^2+2b cos(2pi k/n)). This is a concave quadratic in cosine for b>0, so minimum over all nonconstant modes lies at largest and smallest cosine, reducing the full minimax to two endpoint-frequency curves. At n=3 they coincide and the global maximizers are b=0 or1. Even n>=4: low-frequency A_n(b) increases and antipodal B_n(b)=2(1-b) decreases, yielding the unique crossing b=(sqrt(1+sin^2(pi/n))-sin(pi/n))^2. Odd n>=5: A grows, high-frequency B decreases to b=d=cos(pi/n), then grows; crossing of A and B is b=h-sqrt(h^2-1), h=1+d-c, and the latter B branch cannot beat the crossing. Concavity plus strict inequality excludes extra minimizing modes; expansions yield max gain 4pi/n and factor-two asymptotic versus one-hop gain.
